types.embedding_query_text: AstronomicalObject: A celestial body or phenomenon observed in space. Also called celestial object, cosmic object. Examples: black hole star, little red dots, MoM-BH*-1, black hole stars.

chosen_type.label: AstronomicalObject
chosen_type.definition: A natural object or phenomenon existing in outer space.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class fits celestial objects like black holes or galaxies.

candidates.label: ImageObject
candidates.comment: An ImageObject is a media object creative work representing an image file. Also called picture, photo, graphic, visual. Examples: a JPEG photograph, a PNG illustration, a GIF animation. Distinct from VideoObject, which is a video file, and AudioObject, which is an audio file.

candidates.label: VideoObject
candidates.comment: A media object representing a video file. Also called video file, digital video, movie clip. Examples: an MP4 video, a YouTube video, a short film.

candidates.label: MediaObject
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a media object like an image, video, audio, or text, which can be embedded or downloaded. Also called digital media asset, multimedia file, content object. Examples: a JPEG image file, an MP4 video, an MP3 audio track, a PDF document. Distinct from CreativeWork, which is a broader category for any creative output.

candidates.label: AudioObject
candidates.comment: An AudioObject is a MediaObject representing an audio file or recording. Also called audio file, sound recording, sound clip, audio track. Examples: an MP3 song, a podcast episode, a voice memo, a sound effect. Distinct from VideoObject, which contains visual content.

candidates.label: MusicVideoObject
candidates.comment: A MusicVideoObject, as a MediaObject, is a video file primarily featuring a musical performance or accompanying a song. Also called music video, song video, official video. Examples: 'Thriller' music video by Michael Jackson, a Vevo music video, a live performance video. Distinct from MovieClip, which is a segment of a film.

types.embedding_query_text: Telescope: An instrument used to observe distant objects. Also called observatory, space telescope. Examples: James Webb Space Telescope, JWST, Webb telescope, Webb.

chosen_type.label: Telescope
chosen_type.definition: An instrument used to observe distant objects.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org class for telescopes; HowToTool is too generic.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

candidates.label: WarrantyScope
candidates.comment: An enumeration describing the range of services covered by a warranty in case of product defect or malfunction. Also called warranty coverage, guarantee scope, service level. Examples: "Parts and Labor - Bring In", "Labor - On Site", "Parts Only".

candidates.label: DefinedTermSet
candidates.comment: A creative work representing a collection of formally defined terms, such as a glossary, dictionary, or classification scheme. Also called Glossary, vocabulary, taxonomy, thesaurus, enumeration. Examples: The Dewey Decimal Classification system, a medical dictionary, a list of product categories, a set of industry standards. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a single entry within such a set.

candidates.label: HowToTool
candidates.comment: A HowToTool is a HowToItem that is used but not consumed when performing the instructions for how to achieve a result. Also called instrument, utensil, equipment. Examples: a screwdriver, a mixing bowl, a hammer, a computer. Distinct from HowToSupply, which is consumed during the process.

types.embedding_query_text: Astronomer: A scientist who studies celestial objects and phenomena. Also called scientist, researcher. Examples: Rohan Naidu, Robert Simcoe, Florian Peißker, Naidu.

chosen_type.label: Researcher
chosen_type.justification: Astronomers are researchers; mentions are individual scientists.

candidates.label: Researcher
candidates.comment: A Researcher is an Audience type representing individuals engaged in scientific or academic inquiry. Also called scientist, academic, scholar. Examples: a university professor, a lab scientist, a PhD student, an independent scholar.

candidates.label: Observation
candidates.comment: An Observation is an intangible entity used to specify observations about an entity at a particular time, often quantitative. Also called measurement, data point, recorded value. Examples: a temperature reading, a stock price at a specific time, a survey response. Distinct from QuantitativeValue, which is a specific type of observation with a numerical value and unit.

candidates.label: Occupation
candidates.comment: An Occupation is a profession that may involve prolonged training and/or a formal qualification. Also called profession, job, career. Examples: doctor, engineer, teacher, artist. Distinct from Role, which describes a specific function within an organization or context.

candidates.label: AnalysisNewsArticle
candidates.comment: An AnalysisNewsArticle is a NewsArticle that combines factual reporting with the author's expertise, offering interpretations and conclusions. Also called news analysis, interpretive news, expert commentary. Examples: An article analyzing the economic impact of a new policy, a piece interpreting election results, a report on scientific findings with expert commentary. Distinct from NewsArticle, which primarily focuses on factual reporting without extensive interpretation.

candidates.label: Class
candidates.comment: An intangible concept representing a category or type of entity, equivalent to rdfs:Class. Also called type, category, kind, schema. Examples: "Person" class, "Product" class, "Event" class. Distinct from DefinedTerm, which is a specific term within a vocabulary.

types.embedding_query_text: University: An institution of higher education and research. Also called academic institution, college. Examples: University of Hawaii, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, University of Cologne, MIT.

candidates.label: CollegeOrUniversity
candidates.comment: A third-level educational institution providing higher education. Also called university, college, higher education institution. Examples: Harvard University, Oxford College, Massachusetts Institute of Technology, Sorbonne University. Distinct from EducationalOrganization, which is a broader category for any educational body.

candidates.label: School
candidates.comment: An educational organization providing instruction to students, typically for primary or secondary education. Also called educational institution, academy, learning center, college. Examples: a public elementary school, a private high school, a vocational school, a university.

candidates.label: ResearchOrganization
candidates.comment: A ResearchOrganization is an Organization dedicated to conducting research. Also called scientific institute, research company, academic research center. Examples: Max Planck Society, Bell Labs, a university research department, a pharmaceutical research firm.

candidates.label: EducationalOrganization
candidates.comment: An EducationalOrganization is a CivicStructure that provides education. Also called learning institution, academic body, school. Examples: A university, a high school, a vocational college, a research institute.

candidates.label: ResearchProject
candidates.comment: A ResearchProject is a Project representing a planned enterprise aimed at scientific or academic inquiry. Also called research initiative, study, academic project. Examples: a clinical trial, a grant-funded scientific study, a historical research project, a university-led exploration.

types.embedding_query_text: CosmologicalEvent: An event related to the origin and evolution of the universe. Also called cosmic event, universal event. Examples: Big Bang.

chosen_type.label: CosmologicalEvent
chosen_type.definition: An event related to the origin and evolution of the universe.
chosen_type.justification: No schema.org event type for cosmological events like the Big Bang.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: SocialEvent
candidates.comment: An event primarily focused on social interaction and entertainment. Also called party, gathering, social function, get-together. Examples: a birthday party, a wedding reception, a community picnic, a networking mixer.

candidates.label: FoodEvent
candidates.comment: A FoodEvent is an Event centered around food and drink. Also called culinary event, gastronomic event, food festival. Examples: A wine tasting, a cooking class, a food fair, a restaurant week promotion.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

types.embedding_query_text: ChemicalSubstance: A form of matter with a specific composition. Also called compound, material. Examples: hydrogen gas, oxygen-rich silicate dust, water, hydrogen.

chosen_type.label: ChemicalSubstance
chosen_type.justification: Mentions are chemical substances like hydrogen and water.

candidates.label: ChemicalSubstance
candidates.comment: A portion of matter with constant composition, composed of molecular entities of the same or different types. Also called chemical compound, chemical, substance, molecule. Examples: Water (H2O), Sodium Chloride (NaCl), Ethanol, Oxygen.

candidates.label: Substance
candidates.comment: Any matter of defined composition with discrete existence, which can be biological, mineral, or chemical. Also called material, chemical compound, element, matter. Examples: water, oxygen, penicillin, granite.

candidates.label: BioChemEntity
candidates.comment: A fundamental Thing representing any biological, chemical, or biochemical substance or entity. Also called biochemical, chemical compound, biological entity, molecule. Examples: "A protein molecule", "A specific gene sequence", "A synthetic chemical compound", "DNA".

candidates.label: MolecularEntity
candidates.comment: A biochemical entity representing any constitutionally or isotopically distinct atom, molecule, ion, or complex identifiable as a separate entity. Also called chemical entity, molecule, ion, compound. Examples: "water (H2O)", "glucose", "sodium ion (Na+)", "DNA". Distinct from BioChemEntity, which is a broader category for biological and chemical entities.

candidates.label: DietarySupplement

Distinct from Drug, which is primarily for treating, preventing, or diagnosing disease.

candidates.label: SurgicalProcedure

candidates.label: TherapeuticProcedure

candidates.label: MedicalProcedure
